To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the frequency of clinically significant discordance between clinical teams and testing laboratories in variant classification is similar to that of discordance between testing laboratories, (2) most of this discordance is clinically significant, and (3) clinicians tend to be more conservative in variant classification than laboratories.

(1) there was discordant classification of variants by the clinician ordering testing and laboratories, (2) most of the discordant classifications would affect clinical care, (3) the clinicians’ classifications were more conservative than the laboratory’s classifications, (4) the clinicians’ classification was more often in agreement with the submitter in Clinvar than was the laboratory’s classification, and (5) there was a significant difference in discordance between laboratories.
